Runescape was always a game full of "bots", these were disposable accounts run by gold farmers who would abuse item harvesting for logs, fish, and other basic items. They were always a problem in terms of what was called "real world trade". You could go on the black market and buy gold that these farmers would accumulate. Generally, it was a minority of people who purchased black market gold. Jagex were always strict on RWT since runescape's inception.

However in about 2012, they added what was essentially a slot machine, you would get a free spin each day, or you could buy more spins for real money. With prizes like 200m in game coins, or rare weapons worth several million etc. This was the start of Jagex adding micro transactions and becoming the plague that is real world item trading.

It then started with a cosmetic store, where you could purchase fancy outfits to show your real life wealth, and then more recently moved onto a thing called "bonds". A bond is an item that can be purchased from the Jagex website, which can be sold on the in-game market to others players, which can then be traded for several days membership, or for gold. Meaning a player who doesn't want to use real life money, can become a member by accumulating roughly ~7m coins in game. For each bond sold, someone makes ~7m coins. Essentially, you could buy £1000 of bonds, and "legally" exchange that for instant gold equivalent. So then the gold farmers ceased to exist, because Jagex now controls all of the in-game RWT, except there is now no threat of being banned for buying/selling gold, so many more people started doing that.

The problem this created is that most of the "rare" items, costing upward of 2.1billion coins were being hoarded by people who are using mummys credit card. Being able to get so much gold so easily means that highscores are no longer a badge of honour, there is nothing to be achieved anymore, because while you may have spent the past year training your account, someone has simply purchased gold and done the same thing within a few days.

There was also EXP events, where you would get double exp for an entire day or two. Only problem is, you'd need to stock up on ingredients, like ores, seeds, herbs, bars of metal, or other commodities to be able to actually get any EXP. Along with the ability to simply purchase in game gold from Jagex's store, means that item hoarding now happens with rich players who are lucky enough to let themselves spend real money on in game items. So no effort is required on the RWT-ing players. They literally have an easy ride while every honest player would have to prepare for weeks or months to get the same thing.

Basically, they went against everything they stood for and bitchslapped their honest players over a period of a year, causing most of the original clans to disband and dissapear forever. Many top players since the old days of 2001 when runescape started, have since left because of these game breaking changes.

What's the difference between subverse WorldNews and News and Economy and Economics? Can someone
 enlighten me?

v/news -- I see this as a place to put all types of news, emphasizing what is current. Reddit thinks it should be absolutely current and restricted to domestic (US) news. I think it should be the biggest news section, open to a vast array of submissions.

v/politics -- I see this as a place to put stories which can be analyzed from a political perspective, which again is a very broad area. Reddit thinks r/politics should be a place where over 40 domains are censored, where there should not be much outside the partisan TV mainstream, and where stories must be "domestic" or they will be censored. Yes, this happened to me a few times. The most baffling time was where the story I posted had Obama in the headline. When I sent modmail about the 'filter,' I got no answer.

I do not think either v/news or v/politics should be restricted to "domestic" stories. When the time comes, shortly, someone will make a sub for non-US news and politics.

v/worldnews - I see this as a place where stories should be about outside the US or comparative analyses of different nations or regions. This is a tough line to draw as US news often affects other countries in major ways, so the submitter should consider that and post appropriately. v/worldpolitics will come later.

v/domesticnews and v/domesticpolitics when they arrive might be good places for people who want to have partisan battles, as they currently do in r/news and r/politics.

v/economics - I see this as a place for more numerical or deeper economics research, and a good place to post historical or scholarly articles. I guess I sort of agree with Reddit here, except that I would not make "bureau members" -- especially when they subscribe to schools of economics that have been totally discredited for generations!

SO, the lines are a bit blurry, but my submission history might give you a better idea about the subtle differences.

These are only my perspectives, and I would be hesitant for any of these subvoats to start applying content restrictions.
